title_en: Poesis philosophica (Greek and Latin), [Geneva]: Henri Estienne, 1573: first page of the fragments of Heraclitus
title_el: Ποίησις φιλόσοφος (ελληνικά και λατινικά), [Γενεύη]: Ερρίκος Στέφανος, 1573: πρώτη σελίδα των αποσπασμάτων του Ηρακλείτου
licence: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (Internet Archive item record)
note: The page headed 'ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΗΡΑΚΛΕΙΤΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΕΦΕΣΙΟΥ / HERACLITI EPHESII QUAEDAM. Ex Sexto philosopho'. The scan is only 1531 px wide, so the full page is the download. Imprint from the Internet Archive record ('excudebat Henr. Stephanus', 1573); the place, Geneva, is not printed and comes from the Folger Library catalogue ('[Geneva] : Excudebat Henr. Stephanus, anno MDLXXIII'). Heraclitus' and Parmenides' words survive only as quotations in later authors, so there is no editio princeps in the usual sense: this anthology is the first printed collection of them (Commons calls it the 'first published anthology with presocratic texts'). The scan is a Google digitisation of a copy in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Roma (ex-libris 'Ex Bibliotheca majori Coll. Rom. Societ. Jesu'). The page was identified from the Internet Archive's OCR text, not by looking at the image. The same book's title page is leaf 6 of this scan (archive.org/details/bub_gb_3J54VxKz_XUC/page/n6), and Commons has a separate photo of it from a Bloomsbury Auctions sale (File:Estienne_1573,_Poesis_philosophica.jpg, PD-US).

title_en: Homer, Opera (Greek), ed. Demetrios Chalkokondyles, Florence, 1488: first page of the Odyssey

printer: Printer of the Vergilius (C 6061), for Bernardo and Nerio Nerli, Giovanni Acciaiuoli and Demetrios Damilas
attribution: Public domain; suggested credit: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, 2 Inc.c.a. 2064 l
note: Leaf 251r, where the Gesamtkatalog der Wiegendrucke (GW 12895) puts the start of the Odyssey ('251a m. Sign. AAI: Odyssea'); the BSB's OCR reads the heading 'ΥΠΟΘΕΣΙΣ ΤΗΣ Α ΟΜΗΡΟΥ ΟΔΥΣΣΕΙΑΣ' (argument of Book 1). Date: the colophon says 9 December 1488, but the BSB and GW records add that it was finished no earlier than 13 January 1489 (Florentine dating); Commons' BnF pages of this edition say 1489. Printer as given by the BSB record; Commons calls the Nerli brothers the printers, but the catalogues name them as the patrons. Original 3866 x 5400, 2.5 MB. Alternatives on Commons: two BnF pages of this edition (PD-Art on Commons, but the BnF's own page credits '© Bibliothèque nationale de France', so unclear), and a CC BY-SA 4.0 photo of the Bodmer copy open at Book XIII, the return to Ithaca (File:Homère,_Odyssée,_Fondation_Martin_Bodmer_(Incunable).jpg), a display-case photo of a spread. The brief expected the BSB's CC BY-NC-SA, but this item's IIIF manifest states Public Domain Mark 1.0. Page identified from the catalogue's leaf numbers and the BSB's own OCR text, not by looking at the image.

title_en: Constantine Lascaris, Erotemata, with the Golden Verses of Pythagoras (Greek and Latin), Venice: Aldus Manutius, 1495: first page of the Golden Verses
title_el: Κωνσταντίνος Λάσκαρης, Ερωτήματα, με τα Χρυσά Έπη του Πυθαγόρα (ελληνικά και λατινικά), Βενετία: Άλδος Μανούτιος, 1495: πρώτη σελίδα των Χρυσών Επών
attribution: Public domain; suggested credit: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Rar. 302
note: On the cover the page is cropped to its lower half, from the heading ΧΡΥΣΑ ἔπη τοῦ Πυθαγόρου (the upper half is the end of the Gospel of John). Covers the Golden Verses only. The BSB's OCR shows the heading 'ΧΡΥΣΑ ΕΠΗ ΤΟΥ ΠΥΘΑΓΟΡΟΥ' and the first lines in the lower half of this page; the upper half is the end of the Gospel of John, which this grammar book also prints. The facing Latin page, headed 'CARMINA AUREA PYTHAGORAE', is scan 308; the title page, which lists 'Carmina Aurea Pythagoræ', is scan 4. Dates: the BSB gives 1495; the Lascaris colophon reads 'm.cccc.lxxxxiiii Ultimo Februarii' (28 February 1494 in Venetian dating, i.e. 1495) and GW M17107 gives 28.II.1494/95 to 8.III.1495. Editio princeps of the Greek Golden Verses per a Christie's lot description. Iamblichus' Life of Pythagoras was first printed in 1598 (ed. Arcerius); I found no free scan of it, only a 14th-century Laurenziana manuscript page on Commons (File:Iamblichos,_De_vita_Pythagorica.jpg, Plut. 86.3 fol. 41r, PD-Art, 824 KB). This BSB scan is only 1428 x 2089 (642 KB). The brief expected the BSB's CC BY-NC-SA, but this item's IIIF manifest states Public Domain Mark 1.0. Page identified from the catalogue's leaf numbers and the BSB's own OCR text, not by looking at the image.

title_en: Aristotle, Opera (Greek), vol. 5, Venice: Aldus Manutius, 1498: first page of the Nicomachean Ethics
title_el: Αριστοτέλης, Άπαντα (ελληνικά), τόμ. 5, Βενετία: Άλδος Μανούτιος, 1498: πρώτη σελίδα των Ηθικών Νικομαχείων
attribution: Public domain; suggested credit: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, 2 Inc.c.a. 3161 n-5
note: The BSB's OCR reads 'ΑΡΙΣΤΟΤΕΛΟΥΣ ΗΘΙΚΩΝ ΝΙΚΟΜΑΧΕΙΩΝ, ΤΟ Α. Πᾶσα τέχνη καὶ πᾶσα μέθοδος' (GW gives the Ethics' start as leaf 2a, with a decorative band, 'Leiste'). Original 3556 x 5198, 2.6 MB. Volume 5 of the Aldine Aristotle, dated June 1498 by the BSB (GW 2334: 5.VI.1498), 'Venetiis : dexteritate Aldi Manucii Romani'. This BSB copy has two engraved portraits of Petrus Victorius (Piero Vettori), inscribed 'Romae ex Museo Victorio', bound in after the title leaf, so its leaf numbers run two ahead of the catalogue's; the BSB's OCR also picks up handwritten notes in the margins, so the page may carry annotations. The title leaf, which lists 'Ethicorum ad Nicomachum libri x. Politicorum libri viii...', is scan 5 and would do for either book. The brief expected the BSB's CC BY-NC-SA, but this item's IIIF manifest states Public Domain Mark 1.0. Page identified from the catalogue's leaf numbers and the BSB's own OCR text, not by looking at the image.
